prerequisites: Basic knowledge of vector calculus, integral and differential calculus

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic equations of the tension-compression rod consisting of strain-displacement relationships, stress-strain relationships, and the material properties of linear, isotropic elasticity.
Know the basic equations of three-dimensional linear and isotropic elasticity.
Be able to calculate and understand the deformation and stress state of bending beams under planar and biaxial bending as well as torsion.
Be able to calculate principal stresses and principal stress directions of arbitrary three-dimensional stress states, as well as von Mises equivalent stresses.
Be able to independently dimension tension-compression rods and bending beams (due to tension, bending, and torsion).
Know the problem of stability of columns subjected to compression and be able to calculate critical loads for various boundary conditions.
Know the concepts of work and energy, which are conveyed using elastically deformed tension-compression rods and bending beams.
Students gain subject-specific and methodological competencies for calculating elastically deformable bodies.

syllabus_topics: Bending and torsion of straight beams
assessment_rules: The assessment is based on a 120-minute written exam. This exam accounts for 100% of the module grade.
